observation.visible_scene: A tan, rounded foam- or sponge-like object rests on sandy dirt littered with gray ash (right), white paper debris (left), and scattered pebbles. The front-left portion of the object is blackened and charred, and it is actively burning: a tall yellow-orange flame rises from the left edge, and a lower flame line runs along the top of the charred front face. The camera and the object stay in fixed positions relative to the ground markers throughout.
visible_changes: The tall left flame continuously flickers, changing height, thickness, and lean (sometimes upright, sometimes bending left, sometimes reduced to a small tongue).
The flame along the charred front edge reshapes frame to frame, alternating between a near-continuous line and broken, separated tongues.
Occasionally a small detached flame or ember appears at the upper left (e.g., leaning far left or floating separately), then re-merges or vanishes.
The brown object's overall shape and position remain static; the blackened charred region persists without obvious large change.
Background elements (ash pile, paper, pebbles, dark soil spot) remain in the same positions, indicating no camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the fire was ignited.
The true material identity of the object and of the ground debris.
Whether the object is being progressively consumed or will collapse after this excerpt.
Any earlier or later flame behavior beyond the cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the charred black area slowly expands or merely appears roughly constant.
Whether the floating left ember is a separate burning fragment or just a flicker of the main flame.
Exact fuel source sustaining the flame (surface vs. interior).
